# m.futures.schedules

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The timed events of each futures product's trading sessions.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.futures.schedules(*, product_code=None, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `ProductCode`, `TradingVenue`, `Timestamp` and `Event`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `product_code` | Only this product, such as `"ES"`, or these, such as `["ES", "NQ"]`. A table of them in a `ProductCode` column works too. Leave it out for every product. |
| [`start`](README.md#start) | The first session, by `SessionEndDate`, as a date. |
| [`end`](README.md#end) | The last session, as a date. Leave it out to include sessions still to come. |
| [`sort`](README.md#sort) | A field of the rows. Without it, Massive sorts by `product_code`. Fields: any REST field under [Massive fields](#massive-fields). |
| [`order`](README.md#order) | The direction of `sort`. |
| [`limit`](README.md#limit) | The most rows to return, in total. A table of product codes caps every code's requests instead. |
| [`filters`](README.md#filters) | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"trading_venue": "XCME"}`. Don't pass `session_end_date`, which `start` and `end` set. Keys: `trading_venue`, `trading_venue_any_of`, `trading_venue_gt`, `trading_venue_gte`, `trading_venue_lt`, `trading_venue_lte`. |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Schedules (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Futures Basic | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Starter | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Developer | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Advanced | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CME | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CBOT | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business NYMEX | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business COMEX | Updated daily, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's event time. From REST `timestamp`: "The timestamp for the given market event." |
| `Event` | String | The type of session on the given trading date. |
| `ProductCode` | String | The product code of the futures contract. |
| `ProductName` | String | The name of the futures product to which this schedule applies. |
| `SessionEndDate` | String | The session end date (also known as the trading date) of the session the event belongs to. Trading sessions end at 5 PM Central Time, so a session ending at 5 PM CT on January 1st has a session_end_date of 2025-01-01. |
| `TradingVenue` | String | The trading venue (MIC) for the exchange on which this schedule's product trades. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
